To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
party leaders who have the majority of their parliamentary group behind them are more likely to survive, while the performance of their party is of minor importance.

the survival of party leader in a parliamentary democracy is affected by: 1) political performance of a leader, 2) the rules of leadership succession within a party and 3) the intra party support of a leader.

party leaders survive if they have intra party support (i.e. they have the support of the party elite and the party membership), if they are successful at the polls (winning elections and securing government participation) and if they have a long time in office.
